title: Board of Peace Won't Hold Israel to Ceasefire Terms if Hamas Rejects Disarmament — Critical Diplomatic Shift on Day 942
detail: On May 6, 2026 (Day 942 / Ceasefire Day 209), the US-led Board of Peace made a landmark announcement with potentially decisive consequences for the Gaza ceasefire: if Hamas does not accept the disarmament framework, the Board will not hold Israel to the terms of the October 2025 ceasefire agreement — effectively giving Israel a diplomatic green light to resume full-scale military operations. Reported by the Times of Israel, the announcement marked a fundamental shift in the international position: previously, the Board urged both sides to comply with ceasefire terms while negotiations continued. By removing the ceasefire obligation from Israel in the event of Hamas non-compliance, the Board of Peace aligned itself with Israel's position that Hamas disarmament is a precondition for any durable peace. High Representative Nickolay Mladenov, having met Netanyahu on May 5, delivered the message to Hamas: the Board of Peace's diplomatic protection of Hamas's ceasefire standing would end if disarmament talks were not entered in good faith. Humanitarian organizations expressed alarm — UNRWA, WHO, and MSF warned that resumed warfare would be catastrophic for Gaza's 2.3 million civilians. Egypt and Qatar, who serve as key mediators, expressed deep concern that removing the ceasefire protection from Israel effectively ended their ability to broker agreement. Hamas responded that any resumed Israeli offensive would be met with full armed resistance. The announcement, arriving two days after the Israeli security cabinet formally weighed war resumption scenarios on May 3, significantly narrowed the diplomatic space for preventing a return to full-scale conflict — the third major military campaign following October 2023's Operation Swords of Iron and its ceasefire in October 2025.

media.caption: Board of Peace signals it won't hold Israel to ceasefire if Hamas rejects disarmament — major diplomatic shift, May 6, 2026

title: Israel Now Controls ~60% of Gaza Despite Ceasefire as IDF War Resumption Plans Completed — Day 942
detail: On May 6, 2026 (Day 942 / Ceasefire Day 209), Israeli Army Radio reported that IDF forces had expanded their effective control to approximately 60 percent of the Gaza Strip — despite the October 2025 ceasefire agreement that called for gradual Israeli withdrawal and free Palestinian movement. The expanded military footprint encompassed buffer zones and areas along the south, north, and east of Gaza, confining the Palestinian civilian population to roughly 40 percent of the enclave while Israeli forces occupied the remainder. Senior IDF officers were described as pressing for the resumption of full military operations, with operational plans 'completed' and awaiting political authorization from Prime Minister Netanyahu's security cabinet. The territorial expansion contradicted the ceasefire's withdrawal schedule and added to the 2,400+ documented ceasefire violations reported by the Gaza Governmental Media Office since October 10, 2025. The IDF expansion was directly tied to the broader October 7 aftermath and its unresolved political questions: so long as Hamas refuses to disarm and renounce future attacks on Israel, the Israeli military maintains it must retain a controlling buffer zone as a security guarantee. Palestinian officials said the de facto occupation of 60% of Gaza was forcing families into overcrowded areas with inadequate food, water, sanitation, and medical care — compounding the $71.4 billion reconstruction crisis that cannot be unlocked until governance and security guarantees are established. The May 6 Board of Peace announcement that it would not hold Israel to ceasefire terms if Hamas rejected disarmament further legitimized the Israeli military posture in the eyes of international observers, even as humanitarian organizations condemned it as collective punishment under international law.
